citation: Junan Lin and Tal Mor. (2020). Quantum Candies and Quantum Cryptography. https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.02837
title: The B92 protocol demonstrated with qandies using a single color and a single taste
description: The article adapts the B92 protocol to qandies, where Alice prepares only red and chocolate qandies standing for bits 0 and 1. Bob randomly tastes or looks and publicly announces success or failure, where "the success condition is defined as tasting vanilla or seeing green." Seeing green implies bit 1 because Alice never prepared green and red could not lead to seeing green; vanilla implies bit 0 analogously. As in BB84, they compare a subset of bits to detect an eavesdropper and use post-processing to generate a final key.
requirements: Bob's observation choices are not revealed to Alice; only success/failure is announced publicly
target_learning_goals: understanding the B92 quantum key distribution protocol
examples: Alice prepares only red (bit 0) and chocolate (bit 1) qandies; Bob associates green with 1 and vanilla with 0
